results.title: Auto Parts Tariffs and Repair Costs: What It Means in 2026
results.content: The automotive tariff structure in 2026 is layered, and the layers do not overlap cleanly. Passenger vehicles and auto parts fall under Section 232 national security tariffs at 25%. The parts duty took effect on May 3, 2025. A separate Section 301 authority applies 100% to Chinese electric vehicles and 25% to most other Chinese automotive categories. Vehicles and components that qualify under USMCA rules of origin still clear at 0%. [...] Every collision repair estimate written in the United States today carries a cost layer that did not exist three years ago. Auto parts tariffs, specifically the 25% Section 232 duties applied to imported vehicles and components, have now worked their way through the supply chain and are visible in the line items of ordinary repair orders. For most drivers the effect stays invisible until something goes wrong. Then it surfaces as a higher estimate, a longer repair, and in a growing number of [...] The practical exposure is broad because the American parts supply chain is not domestic. More than 30% of auto parts used in the United States come from Mexico and Canada, and a significant share of electronics, sensors, and control modules originate outside North America entirely. The categories most affected by the duties include engines, transmissions, electrical systems, and advanced driver assistance sensors, which are also among the most expensive components to replace after a collision.

Valeo is a French global automotive supplier headquartered in France, listed on the Paris Stock Exchange (CAC Next 20 Index). It supplies a wide range of products to automakers and the aftermarket. The Group employs 113,600 people in 29 countries worldwide. It has 186 production plants, 66 R&D centers and 15 distribution platforms. In 2018, Valeo's sales rose 4% to €19.1 billion. It frequently ranks as France's leading patent filer.
